indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.2.2.1 Demonstrate understanding of the life cycle of a plant
indicator.objective: Know the materials needed for the survival of plants in the environment (water, carbon dioxide, oxygen, sunlight)

skills.description: Name the materials needed for plant survival: water, carbon dioxide, oxygen, sunlight.
Identify where each material comes from (water from soil/rain, carbon dioxide from air, oxygen from air, sunlight from sun).
Explain the role of water in plant survival (helps make food, keeps plant upright, carries nutrients).
Explain that carbon dioxide is used by plants to make food.
Recognise that plants need oxygen for respiration.
Explain that sunlight provides energy for plants to make food.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Plants only need water and sunlight.
Plants get food directly from the soil.
Carbon dioxide is not needed by plants.
Sunlight is only for warmth, not for food.

questions.stem: Which of these is needed by plants for survival?
questions.explanation: Water is needed by plants for survival.

questions.stem: Which set lists materials needed for plant survival?
hints: Plants need gases from the air.
questions.explanation: Plants need water, carbon dioxide, oxygen and sunlight to survive.
questions.misconception: Plants only need water and sunlight.

questions.stem: Name two materials needed for plant survival.
questions.explanation: Plants need water, carbon dioxide, oxygen and sunlight.

questions.stem: Where do plants get carbon dioxide from?
hints: It is in the air around us.
questions.explanation: Plants get carbon dioxide from the air.
questions.misconception: Plants get carbon dioxide from the soil.

questions.stem: Where do plants get water from?
options: From the soil through their roots
questions.explanation: Plants get water from the soil through their roots.
questions.misconception: Plants get water from the air only.

questions.stem: Where does the sunlight that plants use come from?
hints: It is the brightest object in the sky.
questions.explanation: Plants get sunlight from the sun.
questions.misconception: Plants get sunlight from the moon.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Plants get all their food from the soil.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, plants get food from the soil
No, plants make their own food using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water
No, plants get food from the air only
No, plants get food from rocks
hints: Plants make food in their leaves.
They need sunlight, carbon dioxide and water.
questions.explanation: Plants do not get food directly from the soil. They make their own food using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water.
questions.misconception: Plants get food directly from the soil.

questions.stem: What is one role of water in plants?
options: It changes the colour of leaves
hints: Water is used in making food.
Plants need water to stay alive.
questions.explanation: Water helps plants make food and keeps them healthy.
questions.misconception: Water is not needed for plant survival.

answer: to make food and stay healthy
to help make food and carry nutrients
questions.explanation: Plants need water to make food, carry nutrients and stay upright.

questions.stem: A plant is not watered for many days. What will happen?
options: The plant will wilt and may die
The plant will change colour to white
The plant will produce more flowers
hints: Plants need water to stay upright.
Without water, plants lose their firmness.
questions.explanation: Without water, the plant will wilt because water helps keep plant cells firm and supports the plant.

questions.stem: What do plants use carbon dioxide for?
hints: Plants make food in their leaves.
Carbon dioxide is one of the materials used.
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide to make food during photosynthesis.
questions.misconception: Plants do not need carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Why do plants need carbon dioxide?
answer: it is used to make food in the leaves
hints: Carbon dioxide is used in this process.
questions.explanation: Plants need carbon dioxide to make food through photosynthesis.
questions.misconception: Carbon dioxide is not needed by plants.

questions.stem: A plant is kept in a sealed clear box with no carbon dioxide. What will happen?
options: The plant will not be able to make food and will eventually die
The plant will produce more oxygen
hints: Carbon dioxide is needed for making food.
questions.explanation: Without carbon dioxide, the plant cannot make food and will eventually die.
questions.misconception: Plants do not need carbon dioxide.

questions.explanation: Plants need oxygen for respiration, which releases energy for life processes.

questions.stem: Why is oxygen important for plants?
answer: it is used for respiration to get energy
questions.explanation: Oxygen is important for plants because they use it for respiration to release energy.
questions.misconception: Plants only produce oxygen; they do not need it.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Plants only give out oxygen; they do not need it.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, plants only give out oxygen
No, plants need oxygen for respiration, just like animals
No, plants only need carbon dioxide
No, plants do not need any gases
questions.explanation: Plants need oxygen for respiration, even though they also produce oxygen during photosynthesis.

hints: Plants make food in their leaves.
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight to make food through photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Explain why sunlight is important for plants.
answer: it provides energy for plants to make food
plants use sunlight to make their own food
hints: Plants make food using this energy.
questions.explanation: Sunlight is important because it provides the energy plants need to make food.

questions.stem: Draw a simple plant and label the materials it needs to survive. Show where each material comes from (e.g. water from soil, sunlight from sun, carbon dioxide from air).

Labeled water and showed it coming from soil
Labeled sunlight and showed it coming from the sun
Labeled carbon dioxide and showed it coming from the air
Labeled oxygen as needed by the plant

hints: Think about what plants need to grow.
Show where each material comes from.
